title: RC-10 (b) never-settling operation: a wait() with no timeout runs inside withNonceLock, including the Base/Arbitrum private-path strategy (passthrough tx.wait(3)), so a tx that is never mined holds the wallet lock forever and every later buy and exit of that wallet waits behind it

evidence.note: wallet.sendTransaction, then await tx.wait(3): 3 confirmations and NO timeout argument. The comment at :133-137 says "tx.wait(3) may TIME OUT"; with ethers 6.16.0 it cannot, so the submit closure never returns for a tx that is never mined. This site is not named in ESC-PRE-02

submitWithReconciliation awaits the strategy submit closure with no bound; the bounded confirm window (:576-583) only runs after the closure returns, so on Base and Arbitrum the D-CONFIRM-WINDOW bound never applies to a stuck tx
submitBuyTx holds withNonceLock for the whole sendTxWithRetry, i.e. the passthrough closure above on Base/Arbitrum buys
submitPrivateSell holds withNonceLock for the whole escalatePrivateSell (passthrough on Base/Arbitrum private sells)
partial sell holds withNonceLock for sendTxWithRetry (passthrough on Base/Arbitrum)
deliberate public buy: await stx.wait() with no timeout inside withNonceLock (ESC-PRE-02 site 1; BUY-slice rediscovery AUD-BUY-025)
public-fallback approve: await approveTx.wait() inside withNonceLock (ESC-PRE-02 site 2; EXIT rediscovery AUD-EXIT-009)
public-fallback swap: await stx.wait() inside withNonceLock (ESC-PRE-02 site 3; AUD-EXIT-009)
ensureApproval waits with no timeout; reached under withNonceLock from :871, :874, :1509, :1512 (AUD-EXIT-009)
the next op for the wallet starts only after the prior op settles
Promise.race frees only the caller; the inner op keeps the lock
the anti-rug exit is bounded by withTimeout(WATCHDOG_BUDGET_MS, default 60000, :77-81), so it gives up while its queued sell stays behind the stuck op
the TIMEOUT timer is armed only when timeout > 0; otherwise the waiter settles only on a receipt with enough confirmations or a detected replacement

while the on-chain nonce is below the tx nonce the replacement check returns and waits again, so a dropped tx whose nonce never advances keeps waiting; the replacement scanner re-arms on every block (:1194-1210), so a stuck wait also polls blocks forever (listener leak)

by contrast the Flashbots bundle.wait() (flashbots.ts:317) is bounded by the library TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000 (:406-415), so the ETH private path is long but not unbounded (see AUD-TX-003, AUD-TX-008)

evidence.ref: node tx-lock-repro.js <snapshot> (Node 22.16.0, scratch folder outside the repo; loads the base-SHA snapshot of src/utils/nonceAuthority.ts via typescript.transpileModule plus ethers@6.16.0 TransactionResponse on a fake provider; no src/ import, no SQLite, no .env, no network)
evidence.note: A2 printed "A2 caller: caller freed by race, op still queued" and "A2 after 3000ms: locked wait(3) = PENDING | queued sell ran = false"; the control "wait(3, 800): TIMEOUT after 816 ms" shows the same tx settles when a timeout is passed
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): The native confirmation wait can prevent exit fallback indefinitely

sibling_sites_checked: Every .wait( under src at the base SHA (git grep): passthrough.ts:140 (this slice, under the lock via submitBuyTx / submitPrivateSell / partial sell), flashbots.ts:317 (library bundle.wait, bounded at 5 min), bot.ts:750, exitEngine.ts:422 (via :871, :874, :1509, :1512), :545, :556. bloxroute.ts has no wait (it always reconciles, bounded by MEV_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS). Out-of-process scripts (scripts/recover-sell-ladys.ts:72, :82, scripts/addLiquidity.ts, scripts/deploySepoliaTest.ts) take no in-process lock and belong to the SCRIPTS slice. The BUY rediscovery is AUD-BUY-025 and the EXIT rediscovery is AUD-EXIT-009; this entry is the canonical never-settling sub-finding the EXIT entry pointed to with rc:RC-10. Re-entrancy is the separate sub-finding AUD-TX-001.
severity_rationale: S1, equal to the research suggestion and to ESC-PRE-02. Condition: one public or sequencer tx that is never mined and never replaced (underpriced during a fee spike and then dropped, or lost by a lagging or failing RPC node). New relative to ESC-PRE-02: the Base/Arbitrum private-path strategy itself waits with no timeout (passthrough.ts:140), so on those chains every snipe buy and every private sell is a never-settling site, not only the public fallbacks; and the code comment there states the opposite. Registered as a rediscovery under the existing pre-phase record (one record per item, AC-39), not escalated again.
recommendation: Phase 24 (card TX-01): never wait without a bound while holding the wallet lock. Give every wait() inside the lock (passthrough.ts:140, bot.ts:750, exitEngine.ts:422/:545/:556) an explicit timeout, and on timeout reconcile against chain state (receipt + latest nonce) the way reconcileInclusion does, then decide replace/cancel/keep-waiting outside the lock or with a bounded replacement. Keep the lock until the nonce is settled or explicitly replaced, because releasing it while a public tx is still pending would let the next op sign the same nonce (ethers contract sends take nonce "pending", strategies take "latest"). Prove it in Phase 23 with a never-mined tx on a local chain. Nothing is changed in Phase 22.

sub_claims.claim: Passthrough (Base/Arbitrum) private submits wait for 3 confirmations with no timeout while holding the wallet lock
The three ESC-PRE-02 public-path sites (bot.ts:750, exitEngine.ts:545, :556) and ensureApproval (:422) wait with no timeout under the lock
An outer withTimeout or the worker watchdog frees the caller but leaves the lock held and the later ops queued
